steps.text: Welcome to the tax office! I'll walk you through your first case, start to finish.
Every case starts the same way. Talk to the receptionist to receive today's case.
Good. Your Case Folder is now on your desk, waiting to be reviewed.
See that Notes icon up in the top right? It just unlocked. Open it now — it lists every task for this case and checks them off as you go.
Keep that open in the back of your mind. Whenever you're not sure what to do next, check there first.
A few more things up top: your current phase and the clock are on the upper left, and more icons will unlock next to Notes as you open the Case Folder and Tax Code Book for the first time.
This is the Case Folder — your client's information, income figures, and filing status all live here. It starts mostly blank; you'll fill it in as you work the case.
Tap the left or right edge of the page to turn it, and swipe down anywhere on the folder to close it. No buttons needed.
Now open one of the Supporting Documents on Page 6 — these hold the client's real financial records.
See that value in the document? Click it, then click the matching field in the Case Folder to transfer it. That's how you fill in everything in this game — click a value, click where it belongs.
Documents only tell part of the story. Head to the Client and conduct the interview — you'll need what they tell you to fill in the rest of the folder correctly.
Not sure which category a client's answer falls under? The Tax Code Book has the official classifications — open it and find the matching term.
Numbers and terms shown in a highlighted box are clickable, just like document values — the surrounding paragraphs are just for reference.
Once you've got Gross Income and Expenses into the folder, open the Computer to run the Tax Calculator.
Transfer the income figures into the calculator, then hit Calculate. The results become new draggable values — transfer those into the folder too.
Before you decide anything, check the Corkboard. It lays out every document at once so you can spot inconsistencies.
You can drag documents around the board to compare them side by side, and check the hint notes if you're stuck.
Based on everything you've found, stamp the case Ready or Not Ready for Filing. This is your official verdict — choose carefully.
If you stamped Ready for Filing, the Computer will unlock a new option — Prepare Tax Return. Fill it out the same way: click a value, then click where it belongs on the form.
Once you're confident, submit the Case Folder to the Auditor for final review. Heads up — after this, you can't go back and change anything.
Return to the client and let them know how their case turned out.
Last step — file the completed folder away in the archive cabinet.
You'll see your results next — completion time, whether your verdict was correct, and how many issues you missed. That determines your EXP and Reputation for the case.
That's the full loop — receive, review, interview, research, compute, analyze, stamp, submit, present, archive. Every future case follows the same steps. Good luck!
